summary: Feed s099_single to APM is degraded due to 9.9% duplicate packets (209/2117) exceeding 5% threshold. All other visibility checks (one-way, VLANs, drops, overload, truncation, tunnels, encryption, oversize) are healthy.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker is forwarding the same packet twice, typically from aggregating multiple SPAN/TAP inputs that see the same flow without deduplication enabled (e.g., same traffic mirrored from two switches or both sides of a TAP aggregated to one tool port).
findings.impact_on_tool: APM will double-count transactions and inflate metrics, skew latency/response-time calculations, and waste processing and 10G tool capacity on 9.9% redundant traffic. APM needs both directions but not full payload, so duplicates directly degrade performance analytics accuracy.

recommended_fix.why: Enable packet-broker deduplication on the egress toward s099_single to drop identical packets seen within a short time window before delivery to APM, eliminating double-counting while preserving both directions for transaction correlation.
